messages:
anna: Quick design check — we have a long multi-step form (10+ fields) and want guidance on how validation should behave. Should we show field errors inline as you type, only on submit, or mix with a top banner summary?

kevin: my vote: inline for immediate fields, but a persistent banner for global errors after submit. Long forms need a single source of truth at top so users know they missed stuff. :point_up:

jess: agree with hybrid, but keep inline errors low-key. Red text + icon only when error exists. Avoid scrolling surprises.

samir: edge case: when fields are collapsed (advanced sections) — inline errors can be invisible. Banner should list anchor links that jump to the problematic field.

anna: good call. For collapsed sections let's auto-expand the section when the user attempts to submit and we surface the banner. Animation should be subtle.

kevin: accessibility: any error experience must be announced by screen readers. Use an aria-live="assertive" region for the banner and focus management that lands on the first invalid field.

jess: copy question: banner text — "Please fix the following issues to continue" or "We found problems with your form"? Tone should be direct but not scary.

oliver: prefer "Please fix the following issues to continue" — action-oriented. Also include a subtle count like "3 issues" so user understands scale.

samir: destructive action guardrails — we have a bulk-delete at the end of the flow (delete multiple configured models). Should we show a confirmation modal with typed-confirm or a simple confirm+undo?

anna: typed-confirm is heavy and slows down support workflows. For power users, undo is faster if we have reliable async deletion with an undo window (10s) and clear toast. But for destructive actions that are irreversible (e.g., delete dataset), require typed-confirm.

kevin: proposal: 1) bulk-delete of ephemeral items -> toast + undo. 2) delete of persistent customer data -> modal with typed-confirm. 3) deletion triggered from inside a multi-step form -> show inline inline guardrail near the CTA and also the modal if it's irreversible.

jess: microcopy for typed-confirm: label should include item name and an exact instruction: "Type DELETE to permanently remove 'My Model'." Keep it monospaced for clarity.

aria-bot: accessibility reminder: typed-confirm inputs must have aria-label and should not rely on color alone for state. Also ensure the dialog traps focus and returns it after close.

oliver: UX nit: avoid surprise focus jumps when validation fires on blur. If a user tabs through fields, immediate jumping to first error can be jarring. Prefer to mark inline errors but only move focus on submit or explicit action.

samir: technical constraint: client wants cheap implementation. We can stage: Phase 1 banner-on-submit + inline non-intrusive hints. Phase 2 auto-expand collapsed sections + anchor links. Phase 3 typed-confirm variants and undo backend.

anna: tests we should add: keyboard-only flows, screen reader narration of banner + field announcements, mobile behavior for long forms (sticky submit bar with error count).

kevin: mockups — I'll put three variants in Figma: immediate-inline (errors on blur), on-submit (no inline until submit), hybrid (inline + banner). Put them in the review file and tag @design.

jess: tiny copy tweak: for required marker, ditch the asterisk tooltip cruft. Use "(required)" inline for accessibility and screen readers; visible asterisk can be decorative but include text for screen readers.

anna: wrap-up: consensus is hybrid with banner + inline low-priority hints, stronger modal for irreversible deletes, undo for quick bulk ops, and clear accessibility rules. I'll write up an RFC with examples and acceptance criteria.

kevin: :thumbsup: thanks — excited to see the RFC.
